podcast.body: Released on the Bee Gees' "Children of the World" album in 1976, this song later became part of the "Saturday Night Fever" soundtrack in 1977. It was a number one hit in 1976, and some credit it with establishing the Bee Gees as disco kings. John Travolta specifically rehearsed his iconic dance sequence to this song and insisted on performing it to "You Should Be Dancing" for the film. "You should be dancing. Was it number one hit in 1976?"

This song first appeared on the "Children of the World" album and went to number one in the summer of 1976. It marked the first time the Bee Gees extensively used their now-trademark falsetto. "This is, by the way, the first record with Bee Gees really reaching for it with that now trademark falsetto."

This song was a hit in 1976, performing well in clubs and on radio, and foreshadowed the band's immense dominance of radio and the Billboard Hot 100 in the following year. "as was you should be dancing by the bg's who were a year a year away from dominating radio in the billboard hot 100 in ways never seen before."
